doc.title: Al Gallodoro interviewed by Monk Rowe, Oneonta, New York, December 28, 2005

title: Gambling habit and leaving New Orleans
summary: He lost money shooting dice and stopped when he left New Orleans on July 3, 1933.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: Yeah but then I got in a bad habit, the gambling houses, oh God. Yeah the gambling house. Shooting dice you know.
You mean you were losing money as fast as you were making it?
What was the game of choice at the time? Like blackjack or something?
Dice. I’d win but you’ll lose it at the end. You’ll lose at the end. You’re a big loser at the end.
At the time did you say “I’ve got to get out of this?”
Yeah I finally got out of it when I left New Orleans to come to New York. Matter of fact I’ll never forget the day. July 3, 1933, Southern Railroad on Canal Street.
